capabilities: Render a spiral day-planner chart from a plan written below a nautilus code block in a note
Pin fixed events to clock times and flow flexible tasks into remaining time by line order
Show capacity figures including planned demand, available time, and tasks that won't fit today
Track actual work time with Org-style CLOCK entries and a planned-vs-actual review view
Complete tasks with a timestamp and view charts for past or future days
disambiguation: Not a time-logging or journaling tool despite the name; its core job is a visual day planner, and the CLOCK-based execution layer is optional and off by default.
extras: Not in the Obsidian community plugin store yet; installs via BRAT, manual download, or a shell one-liner. Contains no network code, but with the execution layer on it scans every Markdown file in the vault for CLOCK lines. Includes a Diagnose execution layer command for troubleshooting.
intentEvidence: What this project adds is the Obsidian side: the same engine, fed from Markdown files instead of a Roam graph.
motivation: The author built it to bring the Roam Nautilus Log planning engine to Obsidian, reusing the upstream code unchanged and feeding it from Markdown files instead of a Roam graph.
problem: Obsidian has no day planner that shows explicit time capacity, so an overcommitted day's overload stays invisible instead of being flagged as work that won't fit.

relations.evidence: The direct source of this port is 404KSG/roam-nautilus-log
The Roam extension scaffolding the whole lineage descends from
Fixed the timer memory leak, and added bilingual settings, Bézier connectors and CJK typography fixes
What upstream drew on for compatible CLOCK tracking

summary: Spiral day planner that turns a Daily Note into a capacity-aware schedule where fixed events hold their times and flexible tasks fill the gaps.
